newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA M2 BROAD MONEY UP 4.8 PCT IN MAY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA M2 BROAD MONEY UP 4.8 PCT IN MAY.

text.p: Romania's M2 money supply rose by 4.8 percent in May after a 4.97 percent growth in April, central bank (BNR) data showed on Monday.
M2 -- Romania's measure of broad money supply -- was 41.6 trillion lei at the end of May, up from around 39.8 trillion lei at end-April, or more than double its level last May, BNR data showed.
The broad money's rise was higher than monthly inflation, which slowed to 4.3 percent in May from 6.9 percent the previous month.

Cash in circulation stayed flat at 5.4 trillion lei at end-May, keeping the M1 narrow money -- including currency outside banks and demand deposits -- close to the previous level of 10.1 trillion lei at 10.5 trillion.
Demand deposits went up to 5.1 trillion lei at the end of May from 4.7 trillion in April.

Household savings saw a 11.6 percent rise to 13.5 trillion lei in May, while residents' hard currency deposits inched down to the equivalent of 13.2 trillion lei in May from 13.9 trillion the previous month.
Their stake in May's broad money fell to about 32 percent from 35 percent in April.
